checklist.item: A waterproof membrane is shown under the tile on floor and walls, continuous through corners and into the drain.
checklist.why: Tile and grout are not waterproof.

checklist.item: The floor under the membrane slopes to the drain at 1/4 in per ft (2%).
checklist.why: A flat pan under sloped tile holds water in the mortar bed.

checklist.item: The drain is a clamping or bonded-flange type matched to the membrane.
checklist.why: The drain connection is the usual leak.

checklist.item: Curb or threshold: membrane wraps over it; for a roll-in shower the level change and slope meet the accessibility code.
checklist.why: The curb top is commonly pierced by fasteners.

checklist.item: Backing board is a wet-area type, and movement joints are shown at perimeters and changes of plane.
checklist.why: Gypsum board behind tile fails; rigid corners crack.

checklist.item: Tile, setting material, grout and the flood test are noted.
checklist.why: The flood test is the only check before tile.
